# openobserve_synthetic_locations (Data Source)

Lists the probe locations a synthetic check can run from.

Locations are registered out of band, by running a probe agent or by OpenObserve for its public regions, so they are read here rather than declared. Which ones exist depends on the deployment, so naming one that is not configured has a check rejected at apply time. Read them rather than hardcoding.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "openobserve_synthetic_locations" "all" {}

# `names` is the list of identifiers, ready to pass to a check.
output "all_locations" {
  value = data.openobserve_synthetic_locations.all.names
}

# A private location reads "pending" until an agent checks in, and a check
# assigned to it will not run even though it applies cleanly. This matters as
# much as `enabled`.
output "usable_locations" {
  value = [
    for l in data.openobserve_synthetic_locations.all.locations :
    l.location_id if l.enabled && l.status == "online"
  ]
}

output "locations_awaiting_an_agent" {
  value = [
    for l in data.openobserve_synthetic_locations.all.locations :
    l.label if l.status == "pending"
  ]
}

# What a browser check can run in and against. A run costs devices times
# attempts, so this is also what decides how expensive a check is.
output "browsers" { value = data.openobserve_synthetic_locations.all.browsers }
output "devices" { value = [for d in data.openobserve_synthetic_locations.all.devices : d.id] }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `org_id` (String) Organization identifier. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.

### Read-Only

- `browsers` (List of String) Browsers a `browser` check can run in.
- `devices` (Attributes List) Viewports a `browser` check can emulate. A browser run costs devices times attempts, so this is also what decides how expensive a check is. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--devices))
- `id` (String) Data source ID, the organization identifier.
- `locations` (Attributes List) Every configured probe location. Empty on a deployment that has not registered any, in which case a check has nowhere to run from. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--locations))
- `names` (List of String) Just the location identifiers, ready to pass to a check's `locations`.

<a id="nestedatt--devices"></a>
### Nested Schema for `devices`

Read-Only:

- `height` (Number) Viewport height in pixels.
- `id` (String) Identifier a config references, for example `desktop`.
- `label` (String) Human-readable name.
- `width` (Number) Viewport width in pixels.


<a id="nestedatt--locations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `locations`

Read-Only:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the location is configured as usable.
- `kind` (String) `public` for a location OpenObserve runs, `private` for one of your own agents.
- `label` (String) Human-readable name.
- `live_agents` (Number) How many agents are currently serving this location.
- `location_id` (String) What a check's `locations` references. This is the identifier, not the label.
- `provider` (String) Who hosts the probe.
- `region` (String) Region the probe runs in.
- `status` (String) `online`, `offline`, or `pending`. A private location reads `pending` until an agent registers, and a check assigned to it will not run, so this matters as much as `enabled`.
- `types` (List of String) Check types runnable here, which for a private location comes from what its agents report.
